references.text: Moses assures the Israelites that the Lord will fight for them, which is fulfilled here when the Egyptians realize that the Lord is fighting for Israel.
The song of victory praises the Lord as a warrior and confirms that he fought against the Egyptians.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord their God goes before them and fights for them, just as he did in Egypt.
The Lord fights for Israel, a repetition of the promise fulfilled at the Red Sea.
The Lord fought for Israel, just as he did against the Egyptians at the Red Sea.
The Lord's war for Israel is a recurring theme that originates from the exodus from Egypt.
Joshua reminds the people that the Lord has fought for them, referencing his mighty deeds.
The psalm mentions how God destroyed his enemies, including the Egyptians.
Isaiah refers to the Lord's destruction of chariots and horses, pointing back to the downfall of the Egyptians.
The contrast between the Egyptians' recognition of God fighting for Israel and the Israelites' grumbling fear that God will destroy them.
Continues the same historical account of Pharaoh's regret and the Egyptians' recognition of God's intervention.
Theological parallel: God creates panic in the enemy camp using supernatural sounds from chariots or armies.
The contrast between the Egyptians' potential misunderstanding (32:12) and their actual recognition of God fighting for Israel (14:25).
